solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dim cavalier transformed into high-ranking officer

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of these two words are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dim but swaggering fellow somehow becomes a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges the eleven letters of DIM CAVALIER; 'into' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-admiral is a senior naval rank, just below a full admiral, so a high-ranking officer.

clue.text: Cambridge maybe can offer model when there's change all around

indicators.note: all around tells us the word for change encloses the word for model

parts.note: to change is to vary
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone at Cambridge supposedly may pose as a model, while all about them things keep shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can offer' and 'when there's' are link words; 'model' is a verb here, to pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Varsity is a chiefly British word for a university, and Cambridge is one example.

clue.text: Group with little intelligence stuck in bit of the crossword

indicators.note: stuck in says the intelligence measure is placed inside the crossword piece

parts.note: a clue is one part of a crossword
IQ, intelligence quotient, is a short measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: A group of solvers lacking brains get stuck on part of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small exclusive circle of people, a kind of group.

clue.text: A good forward-looking type, PRO out to be combative

indicators.note: out says the three letters printed in capitals are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a progressive is a person favouring reform and forward thinking
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decent reformer, no longer in favour, turns belligerent.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PRO from PROGRESSIVE to leave GRESSIVE; 'to be' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive and combative are synonyms, both describing a readiness to fight or argue.

clue.text: What makes it hard to see half the errors

definitions.text: What makes it hard to see

indicators.note: half asks for just the front portion of the word for errors

parts.note: errors are mistakes

explanation.surface: A riddle-like question about what clouds vision, half the blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of MISTAKES (eight letters) gives the four needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is fine water vapour in the air that reduces visibility.

clue.text: Rambling rector and his endless prosy style

indicators.note: rambling means wandering aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order
endless says the final letter of his is dropped

explanation.surface: A vicar droning on with his tedious long-winded sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts HIS to HI, and 'Rambling' rearranges RECTOR plus HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speech, often meaning showy or long-winded language, a wordy prose style.

clue.text: Greek character holding a dance

indicators.note: holding means the Greek letter grips the single letter inside it

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person clutches a partner for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Where road branches off north in Italian city by front of garage

indicators.note: in places the compass letter inside the city name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Directions to a junction near a garage in northern Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts the G after the city with N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning is a side road leading off a main road, the spot where it branches.

clue.text: Piece of office equipment made to look fantastic by rep in letter

indicators.note: made to look fantastic suggests the letters are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A sales rep features impressively in correspondence about office kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers REP, IN and LETTER together; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleprinter is an old electromechanical typewriter that sent and received messages by wire, standard office hardware.

clue.text: In the morning horse doing circuit was very hot

indicators.note: doing circuit means the horse goes round the time indicator, enclosing it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A racehorse completing a lap early in the day was sweating.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamed means gave off steam, so was very hot, as of a sweating horse or kettle.

clue.text: Recklessness with ridiculous speed needing control

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the word speed is made absurd by scrambling

parts.note: to ration is to control the supply of something

explanation.surface: Driving with absurd speed calls for some control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' makes DESPE from SPEED; 'with' and 'needing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperation can drive rash behaviour, so it is used for a reckless state of mind.

clue.text: Sloppy Sue, idler, having loads of free time

indicators.note: sloppy means messy, so the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Lazy Sue lounges about with endless spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisured describes people with ample leisure, not needing to work.

clue.text: Boy knocked over when interrupted by idiotic folk on the move

indicators.note: interrupted by says the reversed word is split by the next one going inside
knocked over means toppled, so the word for boy is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy
mad means foolish or idiotic

explanation.surface: A boy is bowled over by a crazy crowd heading somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy knocked over' looks like a fallen child, but 'knocked over' is the reversal signal and 'when interrupted by' the container one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wandering peoples who move from place to place.

clue.text: Absconding with child asleep

parts.note: a kid is a child
napping means having a short sleep

explanation.surface: Running off with an infant while it dozes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping is unlawfully carrying a person off, so absconding with them.

clue.text: Money-collecting scheme brings pence always

parts.note: aye is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A fundraising plan always produces a few pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE (Pay As You Earn) is the British system of deducting income tax from wages; 'brings' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: PAYE is the British tax-collection system taking income tax straight from wages.

clue.text: Absorb meal as it is mashed up

indicators.note: mashed up suggests the food words are crushed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instruction to take in food as it is, once it is mashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To assimilate is to take in and absorb, whether food, ideas or people.

clue.text: Unknown pub in place devoted to luxury

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, one devoted to luxury

indicators.note: in puts the unknown and the pub inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
Y is a mathematical unknown
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A mystery pub in a resort given over to indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a person given to luxury and pleasure, after the decadent ancient city of Sybaris.

clue.text: No matter what happens, it's applying to the whole athletics meeting?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning whatever the outcome

definitions.text: applying to the whole athletics meeting?
definitions.meaning: a rule valid in every single race or field contest of the sports meeting

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally, an event being one contest at an athletics meeting; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless or anyway, whatever comes to pass.

clue.text: Liven up a part of the UK with chum

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom
a mate is a chum or friend

explanation.surface: Bring some life to a corner of Britain with a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring to life or enliven, a synonym of liven up.

clue.text: Plan concealed by bride always

indicators.note: concealed by shows the answer lies tucked inside these two words

explanation.surface: A scheme the bride always keeps hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a plan or scheme in the mind.

clue.text: Bundle of papers, one collected by rough sleeper

indicators.note: collected by means the numeral is gathered up inside the sleeper word

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a homeless person sleeping rough
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A homeless person picks up a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSSER is British slang for someone who sleeps rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents on a person or subject.

clue.text: Order the man to get in cream

indicators.note: to get in means the pronoun goes inside the word for cream

parts.note: the cream is the best of something
he refers to the man

explanation.surface: An instruction for the fellow to fetch some cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or order, as in at someone's behest.

clue.text: Local people's bother has British intervening

indicators.note: intervening says the abbreviation comes between letters of the bother word

parts.note: a trial is a nuisance or bother

explanation.surface: Local folk have trouble because Britain is getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal means belonging to a tribe, the native people of a place.

clue.text: A crowd, mostly relations, in a Swiss party?

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd

indicators.note: mostly means the word for relations loses its last letter

parts.note: kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A gathering of relatives at a celebration in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims KIN to KI; 'in' is a link, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising after a day on the slopes, which a Swiss resort might host.

clue.text: Priest in short trousers?

indicators.note: short means the trousers word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: Levis are a well-known brand of jeans

explanation.surface: A clergyman in shorts?
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Levi founded the priestly tribe, and the name is applied to a priest; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was the patriarch of the Levites, the hereditary priestly tribe of Israel.

clue.text: To understand is to make progress, each learner grasped

indicators.note: grasped says the progress word holds the two shorter pieces inside

parts.note: to rise is to advance or progress
L is the learner sign

explanation.surface: Learning involves progress, each student grasping something.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is to grasp or come to understand something.

clue.text: Description of peninsula in cold place lacking sun

indicators.note: lacking means the star abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: Siberian describes something in Siberia, a famously cold region

explanation.surface: A peninsula portrayed as frozen and sunless.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes the peninsula of Spain and Portugal, the adjective naming it.

clue.text: Giants never somehow able to show a heavenly body

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: The Giants team never manage to produce a star.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening star is Venus seen in the west after sunset, a celestial body.
